answer: Sequential work receipts: each identity must publish a verifiable chain of completed micro-tasks, one per epoch, before it can act again. A falcon cannot skip an epoch, so cloning N identities costs N times the compute, latency, and storage of maintaining one honest chain. Sparrow tasks are cheap but strictly serialized per identity, capping parallel progress. A pearl of withheld work breaks the hash chain and freezes the clone, so attackers pay real time and hardware per identity rather than a one-time fee.
